title: India's New Zealand Tour: Three Formats, Three Questions for Gambhir and Iyer
excerpt: A split-captaincy tour from October 22 to December 1 tests Gambhir's model, Rohit and Kohli's World Cup road, and Shreyas Iyer's leadership audition.
body:
• India's six-week New Zealand tour runs October 22 to December 1 across all three formats: five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests.
  • Leadership is split three ways — Shreyas Iyer captains the T20Is and the last two ODIs, Shubman Gill the first three ODIs and the Tests.
  • Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli feature in both ODI squads, making the 50-over leg the clearest read on their road to the 2027 World Cup.
  • The first batch, including coach Gautam Gambhir and 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, has arrived in Christchurch ahead of Thursday's opener.

India have arrived in Christchurch for a tour that asks three different questions in three different formats. The itinerary, confirmed in squad coverage by Wisden, runs five T20Is from October 22 to November 1, five ODIs from November 4 to 15, and two Tests — Wellington from November 19 and Christchurch from November 27 to December 1. The first batch of the squad, including head coach Gautam Gambhir, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Varun Chakaravarthy and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, touched down in Christchurch, New Zealand Cricket said in reporting carried by SportsGr8.

Question one: Gambhir's split-captaincy model

No single captain owns this tour. Shreyas Iyer leads the 16-man T20I squad with Tilak Varma as his deputy, captains the final two ODIs, and serves as Gill's vice-captain in the first three. Shubman Gill leads the first three ODIs and the Test side, with KL Rahul his Test deputy. Gill, Rahul, Prasidh Krishna and Anshul Kamboj will leave the ODI squad after three matches to prepare for the Tests, which start four days after the fifth ODI. Whether this is succession planning or fragmentation is the tour's coaching question — and it is Gambhir's to answer.

Question two: Rohit and Kohli's ODI road

Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli appear in both ODI squads, in what Wisden noted is a management focus on Test cricket even with the ODI World Cup less than a year away. Kohli leads India's returning ODI batters in New Zealand conditions with 596 runs at 49.66, ahead of Rohit's 437 and Iyer's 346. How the two senior batters pace a five-match series split across two captains is the clearest available signal on their 2027 World Cup roles.

Question three: Shreyas Iyer's audition

Iyer is the only man who captains on this tour besides Gill, and he gets the larger share of white-ball leadership — all five T20Is plus two ODIs. Kumar Kushagra and Yash Thakur earn maiden ODI call-ups for the final two matches, and Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj return to the Test squad, where Rishabh Pant is subject to fitness clearance. For diaspora fans in New Zealand and viewers in the US, the T20Is start at 12:30 pm IST — 3:00 am Eastern — with ODIs at 7:30 am IST and Tests at 3:30 am IST. The tour opens Thursday at Hagley Oval.

New Zealand, captained by Mitchell Santner in both white-ball formats, will field squads built around Devon Conway, Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Matt Henry and Jacob Duffy, with Rachin Ravindra in the ODI group for the first three matches. Conditions will vary sharply across the six weeks — spring pitches in Christchurch, the Basin Reserve's wind in Wellington, and Eden Park's short boundaries in Auckland — which is precisely why a three-format tour remains the hardest examination of an Indian squad's depth.
